intended_object: An absorbent (absorbing) set: a subset s of a module such that for every vector x there is r with x ∈ a • s for all scalars a with ‖a‖ ≥ r. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: `Absorbent M s` means `Absorbs M s {x}` for every x, where `Absorbs M s t := ∀ᶠ a in cobounded M, t ⊆ a • s`. Over a normed field with its norm bornology, a set is in the cobounded filter exactly when it contains some {a : ‖a‖ ≥ r}. So the condition becomes: for every x there is an r with x ∈ a • s whenever ‖a‖ ≥ r, which is the textbook definition of an absorbent set. The definition only needs a bornology on the scalars and an SMul, which is broader than the usual normed-field setting, so it is not too narrow. It is Mathlib's own canonical definition, so there is no separate counterpart.
